newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Highflying EDP seems find point of balance. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Highflying EDP seems find point of balance. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]

text.p: State-controlled utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal seemed to be stabilising around 3,000-3,100 per share after soaring on the first day of trade following its partial privatisation at 2,250, analysts said on Tuesday.
The stock, which had been highly volatile on its debut, was trading at 3,106 escudos at 1240 GMT.
"I think that between 3,000 and 3,100 escudos, EDP could gain some support but anything can happen," said one trader who asked not to be named.
"If (it) breaks 3,000, it could go back to 2,750," said another Lisbon trader.
But analyst James Harrison of Lisbon brokers Midas said he saw 3,150 escudos as a "fair price" for the stock.

EDP has swung between a low of 2,700 and a high of 4,050 escudos in the first session of trade since the government floated off 30 percent of the utility in the largest privatisation yet carried out in Portugal.
The price set at the privatisation was at the top of the range the government had indicated ahead of the sale, with demand heavily exceeding supply for the stock.
By 1230 GMT, two and a half hours after the start of trade in the stock, some 3.6 million shares had changed hands, representing more than a third of total bourse turnover.
Analysts were waiting to see how the stock opened in New York. In London, where the share EPGq.L is quoted on SEAQ, EDP was trading at 3,153.74 escudos, having touched a high of 3,300.

Traders said the huge activity on EDP on Tuesday reflected massive unsatisfied demand for the stock at the privatisation. Many institutional and other investors who failed to get all the shares they wanted were now turning to the open market.
EDP becomes part of the PSI-20 .PSI20, the index on which the Oporto futures contract is based, from July 1.
